narrative:
The model determined that you have a 33% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your employment situation, and the level of savings you currently hold. Your checking account status had the largest impact and worked in your favor: having no checking account is actually quite common among approved applicants (59%). This factor pushed the prediction toward approval. Unfortunately, the other two major factors worked against you. Being unemployed stood out as the second most important reason for the denial. While only about 7% of approved applicants are unemployed, this status strongly increased your predicted risk. Your low savings balance (under 100 DM) was the third most influential factor and also pushed the decision toward rejection, as many approved applicants maintain higher savings.

In short, although your clean checking account helped, your current unemployment and very limited savings created enough concern to tip the overall assessment into the denial range.

You should focus on securing stable employment and building your savings balance before reapplying. Once those two areas improve, your chances of approval are likely to increase significantly. (218 words)
